questions.title: Maximum Toys Budget
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_toys(int price[], int n, int budget)

The prices are given in ASCENDING order. Greedily buy the cheapest toys first: keep taking the next price while the running total stays within budget, and return how many toys were bought (0 when even the cheapest does not fit).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n prices sorted ascending. Line 3: budget.

Output Format:
One line with the number of toys bought.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= price[i] <= 1000, 1 <= budget <= 100000

questions.title: Meeting Count Pre-sorted
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_meetings(int start[], int finish[], int n)

The n activities are already listed in ASCENDING finish time. Greedily pick meetings that never overlap (a meeting may start exactly when the previous one ends): take the first, then keep taking the next whose start is >= the finish of the last taken meeting. Return the count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n finish times (sorted ascending).

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= start[i] < finish[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Jump Game Reach
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int can_reach_end(int jump[], int n)

You start at index 0; from index i you may advance up to jump[i] steps. Greedily track the farthest reachable index while scanning left to right and return 1 when the last index (n-1) is reachable, else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n jump lengths.

Output Format:
One line with 1 (reachable) or 0 (stuck).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 0 <= jump[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Cookie Pairing Pre-sorted
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int content_children(int greed[], int cookie[], int n, int m)

Both arrays are given ASCENDING. A child with greed g is content with a cookie of size c when c >= g; each cookie feeds at most one child. Greedily walk the smallest child with the smallest cookie (two pointers) and return how many children can be made content.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n greed factors sorted ascending. Line 3: m. Line 4: m cookie sizes sorted ascending.

Output Format:
One line with the number of content children.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 5000, 1 <= greed[i], cookie[j] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Deadline Slots Pre-sorted
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int schedulable_count(int deadline[], int n)

Every job takes exactly one time unit and jobs run in slots 1, 2, 3, .... The deadlines are given ASCENDING. Greedily schedule jobs in that order: job i takes the next free slot only when its deadline is still >= that slot number. Return how many jobs get scheduled.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n deadlines sorted ascending.

Output Format:
One line with the number of schedulable jobs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 1 <= deadline[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Minimum Waiting Total
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_waiting_total(int time[], int n)

The service times are given ASCENDING — serving shortest-job-first is the greedy optimum. Compute the TOTAL waiting time: the k-th served customer waits for the sum of all previous service times (the first customer waits 0).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n service times sorted ascending.

Output Format:
One line with the total waiting time.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= time[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Lemonade Stand Change
questions.description:
A lemonade stand sells each cup for 5. Customers pay with 5, 10 or 20 bills and must get exact change in order; the stand starts with no coins. Greedily give change: for a 20 prefer one 10 + one 5, otherwise three 5s. Return 1 when every customer can be served, else 0.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int can_serve(int bills[], int n)

It must process the bills in order, maintaining the stand's stock of 5s and 10s, and return 1 when all n customers are served, else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n bills in customer order (each 5, 10 or 20).

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, bills[i] in {5, 10, 20}

questions.title: Rope Joining Cost
questions.description:
A workshop must fuse n rope pieces into one long rope; joining two ropes costs the sum of their lengths and the cost adds up. Greedily ALWAYS join the two shortest remaining ropes — that minimises the total cost. Return the total cost (joining 1 rope costs 0).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_join_cost(int n, int len[])

It must repeatedly pick the two smallest remaining lengths (scan the array; mark merged entries as consumed), add their sum to the total, and put the merged length back — then return the total.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n rope lengths.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total joining cost.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= len[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Rating Reward Candy
questions.description:
n children stand in a line, each with a rating. Every child gets at least one candy, and any child with a HIGHER rating than an immediate neighbour must get more candies than that neighbour. Distribute greedily with a left-to-right pass then a right-to-left pass and return the minimum total candies.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_candies(int n, int rating[])

It must fill a candy array (all 1s, then fix rising runs left-to-right, then falling runs right-to-left, taking max) and return the sum.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n ratings.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total number of candies.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= rating[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Ferry Max Load Count
questions.description:
A small ferry loads crates one by one until its capacity W is reached; to maximise the NUMBER of crates carried, it always takes the lightest remaining crate first. Return how many crates fit.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_ferry_items(int n, int weight[], int W)

It must sort the weights ascending (hand-rolled sort), then greedily take crates cheapest-weight first while the running total stays within W, and return the count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n crate weights. Line 3: capacity W.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of crates.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= weight[i] <= 100000, 1 <= W <= 1000000000

questions.title: Cashier Note Dispenser
questions.description:
A cashier's till stocks the canonical note denominations {1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000}. Because the system is canonical, dispensing GREEDILY from the largest denomination always uses the minimum number of notes. Return that minimum count for the requested amount.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int note_count(int amount)

It must walk the denominations from 1000 down to 1, adding amount / denom notes and taking the remainder, then return the total note count.

Input Format:
Line 1: the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of notes.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 1000000

questions.title: Lifeboat Rescue Sort
questions.description:
A rescue boat carries AT MOST two people and their combined weight must not exceed the boat's limit; every person's weight fits the limit. To minimise the number of trips, sort the weights and greedily pair the heaviest remaining person with the lightest one whenever the pair fits. Return the minimum number of boat trips.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_boats(int n, int weight[], int limit)

It must sort the weights ascending with a hand-rolled sort, then run the two-pointer pairing (when the lightest and heaviest fit together, save one trip) and return the trip count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n person weights. Line 3: the boat limit.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of trips.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= weight[i] <= limit <= 10000

questions.title: Cookie Distribution Desk
questions.description:
A distribution desk hands cookies to children in a queue: child i is content when the cookie size is at least their greed factor, and each cookie goes to at most one child. Maximise the number of content children by sorting both lists and greedily matching the smallest sufficient cookie to the smallest unsatisfied greed.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int assign_cookies(int n, int greed[], int m, int cookie[])

It must sort both arrays ascending with hand-rolled sorts, then run the two-pointer match and return the count of content children.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n greed factors. Line 3: m. Line 4: m cookie sizes.

Output Format:
One line with the number of content children.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 5000, 1 <= greed[i], cookie[j] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Deadline Job Picker
questions.description:
A scheduler gets n unit-time jobs; job i earns profit[i] and must finish by its deadline (slots 1, 2, ...). To maximise the total profit, sort jobs by profit DESCENDING and greedily give each job the LATEST free slot at or before its deadline; jobs with no free slot are dropped. Return the maximum total profit.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_deadline_profit(int n, int profit[], int deadline[])

It must sort the jobs by profit descending (a paired hand-rolled sort), then fill a used[] slot table scanning each job's deadline backwards, and return the total profit of scheduled jobs.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n profits. Line 3: n deadlines.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum total profit.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= profit[i] <= 1000, 1 <= deadline[i] <= 100

questions.title: Trim Overlapping Bookings
questions.description:
A booking system must CANCEL as few reservations as possible so that the remaining ones never overlap (a booking may start exactly when another ends). Greedy rule: sort by finish time, keep every booking that starts at or after the last kept finish, and everything else gets cancelled. Return the number of cancellations.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_removals(int n, int start[], int finish[])

It must sort the bookings by finish time with a paired hand-rolled sort, run the activity-selection keep count, and return n minus the kept count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n finish times.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of bookings to remove.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= start[i] < finish[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Merge Busy Slots
questions.description:
A calendar merges overlapping busy slots: after sorting by start time, any slot whose start is at most the running merged finish extends that block (touching endpoints merge). Fill the merged blocks into outStart[]/outFinish[] and return their count.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int merge_slots(int n, int start[], int finish[], int outStart[], int outFinish[])

It must sort the slots by start time with a paired hand-rolled sort, sweep merging into outStart[]/outFinish[], and return the merged count m. The harness prints each merged block as "start finish" space-separated on one line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n finish times.

Output Format:
One line with m blocks "start finish" space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= start[i] < finish[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Maximum Meetings
questions.description:
A conference hall hosts the maximum number of meetings: sort the meetings by FINISH time, always take the earliest-finishing compatible meeting (a meeting may start exactly when the previous one ends). Return the maximum count.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_meetings(int n, int start[], int finish[])

It must sort the meetings by finish time with a paired hand-rolled sort (the input is NOT guaranteed sorted), then run the greedy selection and return how many meetings fit.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n finish times.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= start[i] < finish[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Fractional Loot Value
questions.description:
A looter fills a knapsack of capacity W with n items (weight[i], value[i]); items may be taken FRACTIONALLY — a fraction x of an item yields x * value. Greedy rule: order items by value/weight ratio DESCENDING (compare with cross multiplication to stay in integers), take whole items while they fit, then take the best-fitting fraction of the next item. Return the maximum loot value as a double; the harness prints it with 2 decimals.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double fractional_knapsack(int n, int weight[], int value[], int W)

It must sort the items by ratio descending with a paired hand-rolled sort, sweep taking whole items and finally a fraction, and return the total value.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n item weights. Line 3: n item values. Line 4: capacity W.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum loot value printed with 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= weight[i], value[i] <= 1000, 1 <= W <= 100000

questions.title: Minimum Platforms
questions.description:
A station must hold the minimum number of platforms so no train waits: a platform is occupied from a train's arrival THROUGH its departure, and a train arriving exactly when another departs still needs a NEW platform. Sort arrivals and departures independently, then sweep both in one pass counting concurrent trains. Return the peak count.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_platforms(int n, int arrival[], int departure[])

It must sort each array ascending with hand-rolled sorts, then merge-walk them (arrival <= departure grows the occupancy, otherwise it shrinks) and return the maximum occupancy seen.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n arrival times (HHMM integers). Line 3: n departure times (HHMM integers).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of platforms.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= arrival[i], departure[i] <= 2359

questions.title: Balloon Burst Arrows
questions.description:
Balloons float as horizontal intervals [start, finish]; one arrow shot at position x bursts EVERY balloon with start <= x <= finish. Minimise the number of arrows: sort balloons by finish time and greedily shoot each arrow at the finish of the first balloon not yet burst. Return the arrow count.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_arrows(int n, int start[], int finish[])

It must sort the balloons by finish time with a paired hand-rolled sort, then sweep: whenever a balloon's start is strictly greater than the last shot position, shoot a new arrow at that balloon's finish, and return the count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start positions. Line 3: n finish positions.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of arrows.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= start[i] < finish[i] <= 1000000
